learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn how to compare nouns using the Positive, Comparative, and Superlative degrees of adjectives, including tricky irregular forms.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 A mouse is small, a dog is bigger, but an elephant is the biggest! When we want to compare sizes, speeds, or qualities, Adjectives change their shapes like magic. Let's learn the three levels of comparison! 📏

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The Positive Degree is the simple, normal form of an adjective. We use it when we are just describing ONE person, place, or thing, without comparing it to anything else.
The Comparative Degree is used when we compare exactly TWO things. We usually add '-er' to the end of the adjective, or put 'more' in front of long words. We also use the word 'than'.
examples_or_templates: Ria is taller than Priya. (tall + er)
This book is more interesting than that one.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The Superlative Degree compares THREE OR MORE things to show the highest degree. We add '-est' or put 'most' in front. We always use 'the' before it! Some adjectives are 'irregular' and change their whole spelling.
examples_or_templates: Ria is the tallest girl in the class.
Irregular examples: Good ➡️ Better ➡️ Best, Bad ➡️ Worse ➡️ Worst

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ What is the comparative degree of the word 'Happy'?
❓ Fill in the blank: 'That was the ______ movie I have ever seen!'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change this sentence to the comparative degree: 'A cheetah is fast.'
subjective_practice.hint: Compare it to a lion. Use '-er' and the word 'than'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write the three degrees (Positive, Comparative, Superlative) for the word 'Beautiful'.
subjective_practice.hint: It's a long word! You can't add -er or -est. Use 'more' and 'most'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Correct the mistake: 'He is the taller boy in the whole school.'
subjective_practice.hint: If it's the whole school (more than two boys), which degree should you use?

activity_or_assignment.title: 👟 The Shoe Line-Up
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Gather 3 different pairs of shoes in your house. Line them up and write 3 sentences comparing them. (Example: Dad's shoe is big. My shoe is smaller than Dad's. My baby sister's shoe is the smallest!)

chapter_summary: ⭐ Comparative Degree compares two things using '-er' or 'more' (faster).
⭐ Superlative Degree compares three or more things using '-est' or 'most' (fastest).
